newsitem.title: BRAZIL: COFFEE--Brazil trade hopes for larger auctions.
newsitem.headline: COFFEE--Brazil trade hopes for larger auctions.

text.p: Good offtake at this week's Brazilian government coffee stocks auction should convince the government that it is time to start raising the amount offered in its monthly sales, trade and industry officials said.
"At the moment the market is saying that we need more coffee. The internal price keeps going up and up," said Oswaldo Aranha, president of the Brazilian Coffee Exporters Federation.
The government on December 18 sold almost 96 percent of the 90,018 60-kg bags put up for auction, the largest sale so far in the 1996/97 coffee year (July/June).

The domestic roasting industry and exporters have already begun lobbying government officials to start increasing the size of auctions nearer to the current 200,000 bags limit, with some even calling for the limit to be raised.

Sales have so far stayed well below this level as they are supposed to reflect internal supply and given good availability from the recent harvest, there has appeared to be little need to deposit more coffee on the market.
As of January however, roasters see a different scenario.
"Without doubt auctions should increase," said David Nahum, secretary-general of the Brazilian Coffee Industry Association which represents roasters.
"I think we should see sales of 130,000 to 140,000 bags in January, 160,000 bags in February and 200,000 bags from March," he said.

Roasters commented on the improved conditions of this week's auction in which the government appeared to take care choosing coffee warehoused in locations where buyers were confident of quality and cup, said Nathan Herszkowicz, president of the Sao Paulo Coffee Industry Union.
"What we understand is that the government chose more convenient lots to make the auction more interesting," Herszkowicz said.
Prices in the last sale were compatible with those in the internal market, he said.

Coffees for example were sold at around 121 reais, allowing for additional freight and other costs, compared with domestic prices of 127 reais for the same amount, reflecting an "acceptable" difference due to the harvests, he added.

While the government can currently increase sales up to the 200,000 bag limit as it wishes, any decision to open auctions up further should be a matter for the new coffee council which joins the private and the public sector, Nahum said.
The council is still to be installed after a first meeting earlier this week was cancelled but private sector officials are confident that a first session will take place in January.
